properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/23/2023 to REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC in Hamilton Twp, Tioga county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/23/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 986169
Permit API: 117-22124
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/23/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Johnson K 02-135 well site located in Hamilton Township, Tioga County on 2/23/2023 at 0935 hours. The weather was 37 degrees with fog. A layer of snow covered the majority of the site today. An Act 9 sign is located at the site entrance.This inspection was conducted in response to a reported release called in to the DEP by Repsol on 2/16/2023. On 2/16/2023 at 0900 hours, a release of 18.7 gallons of produced water mixed with sand was released to the pad surface and containment from a sand trap. Repsol promptly called in the release to the DEP reporting hotline and began cleanup activities. A Repsol representative provided photos of the cleanup to me via email on 2/22/2023.During today's inspection, the impacted area was observed to have been excavated. All impacted material recovered was placed into containers for later disposal. No evidence of any portion of the release remaining was observed today. Pooled water in and around the impacted area was field measured for electrical conductivity ranging from 160 to 320us/cm. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #370057 is tied to this release within CTS.Based on the reported release of 18.7 gallons of produced water to the pad surface and containment, violations of 35 P.S. 691.402(b), 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), and 35 P.S. 6018.301 are cited against API #117-22124. However, due to Repsol's timely remediation of the reported release, these violations are considered immediately corrected at this time. Violations from a previous issue cited on 8/10/2022 and 9/2/2022 remain outstanding against API #117-22124. I departed the site at 1100 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: At time of inspection, 78 degs. and sunny. There are (5) wells on this pad. They are the Jack 1H, 2H, WYO 3H, WYO 4H and the WYO 5H, all are set up for automated production. The (13x9) and (9x5) annulus vents are plumbed to surface w/ 2" pipe and tied into a 2" common pipe venting to the prod. tank with the exception of the 2H, which is a (2) string well and only has the (9x5) annulus plumbed to vent via Sentry valve, the (20x9) annulus has an open top. The (9x5) annulus vents are open and venting to production tank. The (13x9) annuli are plumbed to vent via Sentry valves and the WYO 4H (20x13) annulus is plumbed to vent via Sentry valve. The cellars had water in them w/ no active bubbling observed during insp. An ALTAIR 5X gas meter (cal. 7/2/25) was turned on to check for gas at Sentry valves, cellars, at the well heads and left on during walk around pad and prod. equipment. The only Sentry valve that had gas was the 1H (13x9), LEL: 100% and 18% CH4. No gas was detected in the ambient air. - Individual well pressures listed below were all taken off SCADA gauges: - 1H - prod. tree top press.: 473.5 psi., prod. csg. press.: 539.5 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 0 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 0 psi., and prod. line press.: 421.3 psi. (OUTST) - 2H - prod. tree top press.: 432.4 psi., prod. csg. press.: 382.9 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 0 psi. and prod. line press.: 430 psi. - 3H - prod. tree top press.: 455 psi., prod. csg. press.: 509.3 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 0 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 0 psi., and prod. line press.: 433.1 psi. (OUTST) - 4H - prod. tree top press.: 431.0 psi., prod. csg. press.: 470.1 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 0 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 0 psi., (20x13) annulus press.: 0/psi. and prod. line press.: 419 psi. (OUTST) - 5H - prod. tree top press.: 425.7 psi., prod. csg. press.: 229.0 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 2 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 0 psi., and prod. line press.: 422 psi. - There is a self contained on site compressor on the pad and running at time of inspection. - There is self contained ancillary equipment on the pad. - No other obvious concerns or new violations noted.

Comments: On July 28, 2025, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to a brine release on site (IRs 4021773 and 4021856).Act 9 sign is present on site. Well is tagged. No spills, leaks or releases are observed at the well head at this time. Well site is adequately vegetated in the areas not being excavated, no E and S issues are observed. Upon arrival to the site, the Department observed multiple trucks on-site as impacted material is currently being removed from a stockpile on the North side of the tank and secondary containment. The impacted material is being loaded into the trucks and hauled off site. The area immediately downslope of the site to the access road appears to have been excavated at this time (Photos 4-5, 24-25).Tarp remains installed in the area from the site to the culvert inlet (Photos 9-13, 18-20), however it appears that the stockpile of excavated material from the pit has been removed.Tarps and BMPs remain installed and appear to be in the same condition as noted in IR 4021773 (Photos 6-8, 14-17).Glenn Wilson (Diversified) arrived on-site during the inspection. Wilson informed the Department of the following:- The tarp that was covering the slope immediately downslope of the site was moved to the North side of the site.- The stockpiled material from the pit was moved and placed on top of this tarp. - The slope immediately downslope of the site was excavated and also placed on the tarp.- All of this material is what is being removed from the site today. - No work has been done on the other side of the access road today, including probing for specific conductivity. - Operator plans to remove and replace the secondary containment on site.- Operator has a representative from the tank company on site today to assess if the tank will need to be replaced as well. - Site will be covered back up by tarp following today's material removal.Violations for the brine release remain outstanding.

Comments: Follow up inspection of the County of Cambria Brzez/Hum 3 well conducted on 1/12/2024. Arrived on location at 09:51. Violations were issued on 3/23/2022, 9/22/2022, and 5/2/2023 site inspections for the following: OGA3220(A) - Failure to plug an abandoned well. 78.91(a) - Failure to plug an abandoned well. 78.103 - Failure to monitor well granted Inactive Status on an annual basis and submit monitoring reports. 78.104 - Failure to meet the terms of Inactive Status. 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect each well for compliance with requirements. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit Mechanical Integrity Report to the Department. OGA3211(G) - Failure to post the permit number and operators info at the well site. OGA3211(H) - Failure to install the permit number on the well upon completion in a permanent manner. This 1/12/2024 follow up inspection found that the well remains in a similar condition as the previous inspections. Violations were not addressed or responded to. Well is not equipped for production. Pumpjack, meter, and electric boxes remain on site. Much of the equipment has been dismantled. Wellhead is no longer tied inline. No permit number or operator ID found on the well. Wellhead and much of the equipment is overgrown with trees/brush. Well status was previously approved as Regulatory Inactive. Regulatory Inactive status expired on 04/15/2020. Operator failed to plug or return the well to active status. Review found no annual integrity monitoring reports submitted to the Department. Annual Production Reports have been submitted with 0 production shown for at least the last five years. All of the above violations remain outstanding.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's DCNR 587 02-003 well site located in Ward Township, Tioga County on 2/1/2023 at 1540 hours. The weather was 26 degrees with clear skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a reported release called in by Repsol.On 2/1/2023 at ~1335 hours, a release of ~5 barrels of produced water, ice and sand was discovered by Repsol after a line on a sand trap froze and split. Water, ice and sand was release to the pad surface near the wellheads onsite (photos #1 and 2). Sand, ice and dirt was recovered and placed in a 55-gallon drum for later disposal. The release mixed with onsite stormwater that was held in and around the well cellars. An onsite vacuum truck recovered a reported 1000 gallons of stormwater mixed with the produced water from the cellars and impacted area. I field measured all of the fluids in and around the impacted area for electrical conductivity utilizing an Oakton PCTS 50 meter. All readings ranged from 400 to 680us/cm today. Based on the reported release of ~5 barrels of produced water to the pad surface, new violations of the following are cited against API #117-22101 at this time:35 P.S. 691.402(b)25 Pa. Code78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.301Violations cited against API #117-22101 on 7/27/2022 remain outstanding at this time. I departed the site at 1615 hours.

Comments: On 12/23/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 33 degrees, overcast and lightly snowing when I arrived on location. Snowfall had impacted the region in the last 24 hours, depositing approximately 3 inches on the location. The original south pad for the Taft 851 1V well has been returned to original grade. The plugged well monument witnessed during previous inspections was not visible. Stormwater diversion berms have been installed north and west of the original pad. Due to snow cover, stabilization could not be assessed for the constructed areas. Patterson drilling rig #805 has been towered down and removed from the north pad, having drilled eight new gas wells to total depth. Most of the drilling equipment has been removed from the site. Crews were on site, cleaning up the surface of the drilling mats and pumping out the well cellars. 40 frac tanks, seven rolloff dumpsters, two vac boxes, and four cement silos remain on site. Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Sand separators and two frac tanks remain attached to these wells. I did witness a 4' x 16' x 2" deep puddle of liquid on the unprotected pad surface north of the five GPUs that field tested at 1953 uS conductance. I reported this to a maintenance worker who relayed it to the Seneca site manager, Cory Miller.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water/ice. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1600 hours.

The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the perimeters of the well site were observed to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues.At the time of this inspection, there appeared to be rain water puddles in the area of the previous release and scraping of contaminated gravel. These readings were found to be comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.67mS.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding at thus time pending the Act 2 Final report submittal, receipt, review, and approval by the Department's Environmental Cleanup and Brownfield Program.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/01/2026 to REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC in Pike Township, Bradford county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/25/2026
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8269637
Permit API: 015-23994
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/01/2026
Comments: On 04/01/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County. The weather was 55 degrees and cloudy. Rain fell on the pad within the last 24 hours. I arrived at 0930 hours. The DEP met with Repsol representative Ralph Babcock onsite. We traveled the area of the impact together. There are still two 24/7 water trucks onsite actively recovering fluids. Fluids above the release point were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) at ~1080 us/cm (1 us/cm = 0.001 mS/cm) (photo #2). Those fluids continued traveling through the stormwater ditch into the active sumps (photo #3 and 4). They have excavated up to feet of material was removed from the ditch. The EC of fluids within the sump #1 and 2 was ~1.2 mS/cm. At that time Repsol instructed the truck operator to move his hoses below the sumps to start recovering those fluids which measured ~3.10 mS/cm (photo #5). The EC of the fluids that were directly entering the stormwater basin were ~540 us/cm. The stormwater basin has a containment in place (photo #7). Fluids were being recovered on top of and below the containment. ~60 barrels had been recovered today from the stormwater basin and sump #3. The EC of the fluids directly downgrade of the stormwater basin outlet and before sump #3 was ~5.1 mS/cm. The EC of fluids located below sump #3 was ~6.38 mS/cm. Brow/black vegetation was observed in that area (photo #11 and 12). We traveled downstream and the EC of the fluids were ~1.4 mS/cm. A spring intercepted the path of the flow from above grade. The EC of the fluids downstream of the spring was ~1.2-1.4 mS/cm. The EC of the marsh area was ~1.5 mS/cm. The EC of the UNT to Rockwell Creek upstream of the impacts was 25.3 us/cm (0.0253 mS/cm). Fluids entering UNT to Rockwell Creek at the upper confluence were field measured for EC at 2.4-2.7mS/cm (photo #18). From the upper confluence of the impact to the wetland inflow EC was 185.9- 225 us/cm (0.1859 -0.225 mS/cm) (photo #19). The EC of fluids from the UNT Rockwell Creek downstream impact was 379 us/cm.Repsol stated the stimulation activities for API #015-23994, 23995, 23996, 23997 and 23998 are scheduled to begin on 04/16/2026. Violations against API #015-23994 remain open at this time. I departed at 1100 hours.

Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

The permit was renewed by RE Gas in 2017 and is set to expire on 09/15/2022. None of the earthwork proposed in the plan was ever implemented in the field. The location consists of one very large well location and a separate tank pad. The location is overgrown and clearly has not been tended to in any way for some time. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/17/2024 to GREYLOCK PROD LLC in Hector Township, Potter county. 78a64a(f) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Operator failed to remove regulated substances that escaped from primary containment or otherwise spilled onto secondary containment as soon as possible and inspect the secondary containment after removal.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: GREYLOCK PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/17/2024
Violation Code: 78a64a(f) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Operator failed to remove regulated substances that escaped from primary containment or otherwise spilled onto secondary containment as soon as possible and inspect the secondary containment after removal.
Violation ID: 8211211
Permit API: 105-21962
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Hector Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/17/2024
Comments: On 12/17/2024 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1000 hours, weather was 45F and sunny. An Act 9 sign and well permits are visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Hydraulic fracturing activities remain ongoing onsite and are estimated to be completed near the end of next week. Equipment to support well stimulation remain onsite and all equipment which is required to be held in containment was observed in secondary containment structures (photos #2-6)This inspection was conducted in response to a release of produced fluids from secondary containment reported by Greylock on 12/13/2024 at 0245 hours (CTS #385788). The cause of the release was determined to be a hydraulic fracturing pump which leaked produced fluids that accumulated and overtopped from secondary containment; the release has been contained. Contaminated material was already removed and backfilled by my arrival onsite (photo #7). The soil in this area field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at ~40us/cm. Standing fluids were observed near the area of the release and field measured for EC at ~1140us/cm. Two vacuum trucks for removing fluids have been stationed onsite and were sent to remove the fluids from this area. Greylock took corrective action after this release and rebuilt the entire containment berm and rig-matting system with an 18-inch wall for increased capacity and to prevent additional releases (photo #8).The low points of the produced fluids offload containment structure which was the site of the release on 12/09/2024 (Inspection Report #3881391) have been repaired and a pump has been installed to continuously remove fluids from this containment structure as they accumulate (photos #9-11).The drainage system which was conveying fluids and diesel into the site's infiltration basin on 12/09/2024 (Inspection Report #3881391) remains shut in and a pump has been installed to remove accumulating fluids. No fluids were observed entering the basin at the time of this inspection (photo #12). Contaminated materials have not yet been excavated from the basin as per my previous recommendation to follow Act 2 remediation guidelines (photo #13).The DEP recommends the following:-Continuing to remove fluids as they accumulate in secondary containment structures.-Continue following Act 2 remediation requirements for the ongoing remediation efforts onsite, including those set to take place in the infiltration basin.-Continuing daily secondary containment inspection.No additional violations noted at this time. The violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962.I departed the site at 1100 hours.

Comments: On June 9 2026, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Penn-Glenn 1 OG Well. A Notice of Intent to Plug was submitted on June 1 2026.The findings are as follows:Upon arrival to the site and prior to conducting the inspection, the Department spoke with plugging supervisor Jim Barnes. Mr. Barnes stated that the plugging rig was currently broken and at a shop being fixed and plugging would continue later in the week. Mr. Barnes then left the site prior to the Department conducting the inspection.At the time of the inspection, the well site was located in a gravel lot adjacent to a building located in an industrial yard (Old World Industries). A well head and plugging equipment were observed. The well did not appear to be posted in accordance with OGA3211(G) and OGA3211(H) as the Department did not observe a well tag or well posting onsite. The Department also did not observe a mailbox or other container onsite with any plugging/disposal/E and S documents associated with the plugging of the well.There were no observed fluid leaks or discharges on the ground or around the well at the surface. There were no observed fluid leaks or discharges on the ground observed from any of the additional plugging equipment onsite.An E and S Plan is required to be developed, implemented, and present onsite as earth disturbance has exceeded 5,000 square feet. While earth disturbance did not appear to exceed 5,00 square feet at the time of the inspection, the Department recommends the operator insure an E and S Plan be developed, implemented, and present onsite if earth disturbance exceeds 5,000 square feet at any point during plugging operations.Prior to leaving the site the Department called Mr. Barnes and left a voicemail informing him of the Department's observations and recommending a well posting/tag be installed during the duration of plugging activities as well as to ensure any required documents are present and accessible onsite.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to properly post the well as described above.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/17/2025 to CNX GAS CO LLC in Richhill Township, Greene county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CNX GAS CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/17/2025
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8238341
Permit API: 059-27945
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Richhill Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/17/2025
Comments: On 6/17/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the RHL-71 Well site in response to a spill that was reported to the Department on 6/14/2026 (CTS: 389879).On 6/14/2025 CNX reported a reportable release. The release occurred at the RHL-71 Well site when a pin hole formed in the common dump line between the Gas Processing Units (GPUs) J and K. This caused approximately 84 gallons of production fluids to spill onto the well pad. The spill is reportedly contained to the well pad and no waterways or drainage basins were impacted. Clean up began immediately.CNX will be remediating the spill in accordance with Act 2 guidelines.The following was observed during the inspection:Remediation and clean up efforts were still on going (Photo 1).The impacted area was observed through out the GPUs (Photos 2-5). The common line where the pin hole formed was between the J and K units, the part was replaced (Photos 6-7).Sumps were dug in between some units to capture additional elevated fluids through out the Act 2 process (Photos 8-9).Conductivity readings were taken outside the designated spill area. The readings were not elevated (Photo 10).Conductivity readings were taken through out the spill area. The readings in the sumps and in between the J and K units were elevated, but other readings in the spill area were not (Photos 11-16).Act 9 sign was present (Photo 17).Violations are being issued for the Act 2 release.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Donegal Township, Washington County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/13/2025 to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Donegal Township, Washington county. 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect  brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/13/2025
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8224740
Permit API: 125-29141
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Donegal Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/13/2025
Comments: On 03/13/2025 an Incident Response inspection was conducted at the DMC Well Site in response to an operator reported release.On 03/13/2025 Range Resources Representative, Dennis Furmanek, reported an approximately 84-gallon release of frack fluid off containment at the DMC Well pad located in Donegal Township, Washington County.Range Resources representative, Matthew Dorsey, was on site at the time of inspection. Mr. Dorsey informed the Department that the release was discovered today (03/13/2025) at approximately 5:00 am, that the quantity released was approximately 84 gallons, and that some of the fluid had since been removed via vacuum truck. The source of release was determined to be a hole in the manifold of a blender, located on the southwestern side of the well pad. The release occurred from the damaged blender, filled and overtopped the primary containment, filled and overtopped the secondary containment, and was release onto the pad aggregate. Mr. Dorsey stated that the cleanup will commence after the frac is completed and equipment is removed in approximately 8 days.Range Resources representative, Dennis Furmanek, contacted via phone call to provide updates. Mr. Furmanek stated that a large sump will be dug behind the spill site on the southwestern end of the well pad to collect any remaining fluids and remediation will begin next week after tear down is complete. He stated that he would notify the Department when the cleanup will begin.Mr. Furmanek also stated that he believed the elevated readings that were obtained from the driving lane on the eastern side of the pad and near the site entrance were caused from road salt that had been tracked onto the site from the large number of sand trucks. He stated that the area in which the elevated readings were observed was the same area in which the sand trucks consistently traveled and parked. He also stated the area had recently been sprayed with water to reduce the dust, which would explain the mud observed in those areas that were exhibiting elevated conductivity.Conductivity probe calibrated on 03/13/2025.The following was observed during the inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance. Various co-operations were taking place at the time of inspection and frac equipment was observed on site (Photos 1-2).-Large amounts of pooled fluid and mud were observed on a driving lane near the site entrance on the eastern side of the well pad. Elevated field conductivity readings of 3.37 ms/cm and 4.43 ms/cm were observed (Photos 3-8).-The mixer where the release originated, the secondary containments, and the surrounding areas were observed. The extent of impact could not be determined because much of the impacted area was located beneath the secondary containment. A small sump and hose were observed, located in the impacted area beneath the white plastic sheeting covering the temporary waterline. Field conductivity screening was conducted throughout the impacted area. Elevated field screening values ranged between 4.29 ms/cm and greater than 20 ms/cm. The discharge onto the ground and failure to dispose of fluids, specifically produced fluid, are violations of 78a.54, 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act (SWMA) 301. The potential to have indirectly impacted Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC) is a violation of 91.34(a) (Photos 4-16).-Pooled fluid was observed in tire tracks near the site entrance. Field conductivity screening was conducted throughout the area. Elevated field screening values of 2.48 ms/cm and 2.93 ms/cm were observed. Non-elevated field conductivity screening values of 78.5 s/cm and 1,189 s/cm were observed on either side of the temporary water line (Photos 17-20).Determination:Violations issued.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/03/2025 to APOLLO RESOURCES LLC in Dunbar Township, Fayette county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: APOLLO RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/03/2025
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8251171
Permit API: 051-23285
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Dunbar Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/03/2025
Comments: On October 3 2025, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Nelson 2 OG Well in Dunbar Township, Fayette County in regard to violations issued under IR 3888353.At the time of the inspection, the well appeared to be equipped for production. The well posting was present at the time of the inspection. The access road appeared stable with no signs of erosion or sedimentation issues. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth.The previously observed release from the well head appeared to be active at the time of this inspection. The Department observed fluid actively dripping from the well head onto the gravel beneath it. While the previously observed orange-stained gravel around the well appeared to be visually remediated, a fluid leak still appeared to be active. A background soil conductivity reading was 0.05mS. A conductivity reading was taken of the fluid leaking from the well head with a reading of 4.11mS. A conductivity reading of fluid that has accumulated within the well casing was OR (over detectable range, >20.00mS).The Department previously requested the Operator evaluate the releases that have occurred and provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred. No response has been received, therefore the Department is again requesting the aforementioned information.Based on today's inspection, violations remain outstanding for the observed release onsite.
